De novo diverse seeds (random, greedy algebraic, cyclic orbits) with cheap annealed softmax-Adam screening and L-BFGS plus trust-region LP only for three diverse finalists under a global clock.
direction: Run a genuinely de novo global search over structured seed families instead of starting every trial from the record, using many cheap relaxations and reserving LP for only a few finalists. Generate three seed types: (a) 30 purely random configurations, (b) greedy maximin selections of 73 vectors from algebraic pools such as normalized two-nonzero vectors $(\pm e_a\pm e_b)/\sqrt2$ in $\mathbb R^{13}$ and sign/permutation variants, selecting pool members sequentially by smallest maximum dot product with those already chosen, and (c) cyclic-orbit seeds in which 5 generic vectors are expanded by all 13 coordinate cyclic shifts to give 65 points, completed by 8 greedily chosen hole points. Relax each seed cheaply with a vectorized Adam or momentum method on an annealed LogSumExp/Riesz-type repulsion objective for at most about 2 seconds each, rank seeds by true maximum cosine while also keeping at least one seed from each family for diversity, then give only the best 3 seeds a LogSumExp L-BFGS refinement and at most 15 seconds each of LP polish. Use a single global clock with a 165-second cutoff, never start a new LP unless enough time remains for it, and return the best fully evaluated $(73,13)$ array seen at any point.

idea: Balanced basin-hopping with void reinsertion, coherent-cap shakes and many cheap annealed soft-max repulsion relaxations plus one final trust-region LP squeeze to find an equitable active topology.

Sequential feasibility minimization of sum-squared excess over targets 0.2065/0.2055/0.2045 with analytic L-BFGS gradient from record perturbations, chaining feasible points and finishing with LP/LogSumExp polish.
direction: Replace direct minimization of the maximum by a sequence of feasibility problems at target cosines below the record, which breaks the huge tie set because pairs below target exert no force. For targets $\tau = 0.2065, 0.2055, 0.2045$ in succession, minimize $F_\tau(X)=\sum_{i<j}\max(0,\langle x_i,x_j\rangle-\tau)^2$ over normalized rows using L-BFGS with the analytic gradient obtained by putting weights $2\max(0,\langle x_i,x_j\rangle-\tau)$ into a symmetric matrix $W$ and using $WX$ projected tangentially; start each target from the record perturbed by Gaussian noise of scales 0.01, 0.03 and 0.08, run at most 250 L-BFGS iterations per start, and move to the next lower $\tau$ whenever $F_\tau$ falls below about $10^{-10}$. If any run reaches $F_\tau\approx 0$, its true maximum is at most $\tau$ and is a new record, so polish it briefly with LP; otherwise use the lowest-$F_\tau$ endpoint as a differently stressed seed for one short LogSumExp polish. Enforce a hard 165-second deadline, evaluate the true maximum after every stage, and return the incumbent immediately when time expires.

idea: Large-neighborhood cap surgery deleting 10-16 points and greedily rebuilding with massive sampling plus block L-BFGS
direction: Perform large-neighborhood surgery on a whole spherical cap rather than perturbing all points or moving one point. Choose a cap center in rotation among the rattler direction, a random existing point, a highly contacted point, and the most isolated PCA-projection outlier; delete the 10–16 points nearest that center and freeze the remaining points as fixed obstacles. Rebuild the deleted block greedily one point at a time: for each vacancy sample about 80,000 candidate unit vectors, score each by its maximum dot product with all frozen and already rebuilt points, refine the best few candidates by local soft-max minimization, and insert the winner; after all vacancies are filled, optimize only the rebuilt block variables (with frozen points included as constant obstacles in the LogSumExp objective) for a few hundred L-BFGS iterations, then unfreeze everything for a 1-second smooth relaxation. Compute the true maximum, run LP polish for at most 6 seconds only if the candidate is within 0.001 of the incumbent or better, and accept the surgery only on genuine improvement; cycle through different centers and cap sizes until 150 seconds, always preserving and returning the best configuration encountered.

Break the single-active-pair bottleneck by balanced annealed LogSumExp Riemannian Adam that equalizes the ~1e-6 second-tier gap, seeded from the incumbent plus a tiny shake, finished with a short trust-region LP squeeze.
Symmetry-first search with C12 six-orbit plus pole and C13 five-orbit plus free points optimized in reduced template space by annealed LogSumExp L-BFGS then symmetry breaking and final LP polish.
direction: Search first in a symmetry-constrained orbit space, then release the symmetry. For example, let \(C_{12}\) cyclically permute the first 12 coordinates while leaving the 13th fixed; choose six generic template vectors, generate their six 12-point orbits, and add the invariant point \(e_{13}\), giving exactly \(6\cdot12+1=73\) points. Optimize only the six templates with an annealed LogSumExp objective, using several random template initializations, because the reduced problem has far fewer variables and automatically produces balanced contact loads. Afterwards break the symmetry with perturbations of sizes \(10^{-4}\)–\(10^{-2}\), run unconstrained smooth optimization, and reserve one final LP polish; enforce a hard internal deadline near 150 seconds. Also test a five-orbit \(C_{13}\) construction supplemented by eight free points if time permits.

idea: Iterative rattler-hub surgery that removes the max-pair hubs plus random rattlers, freezes the core, samples 20k+ holes for greedy joint reinsertion and refines with exact-max Riemannian Adam, accepting only unpolished improvements before one final LP squeeze.
direction: Perform targeted surgery on the jammed core rather than random whole-configuration kicks. Identify the zero-contact rattler and the highest-contact or highest-dual-stress hub points, remove the rattler together with two to four hubs, freeze the remaining points, and jointly re-optimize the removed points on their spheres against the frozen core and one another. Generate candidate placements from at least 20,000 random hole samples, refine the best candidates with SLSQP or hinge-loss Adam using the exact maximum as the objective, and test many such cheap replacements without invoking the full LP. Accept a surgery only if it lowers the unpolished global maximum, then give the best accepted configuration one short LP polish; this directly attempts to eliminate overloaded hubs and activate the wasted rattler.

idea: Discrete lattice-pool greedy selection with swap repair to find a fresh topology, then annealed softmax Riemannian Adam and LP polish
direction: Construct a completely fresh configuration by selecting 73 points from a large discrete lattice-like pool before continuous optimization. Generate a few hundred thousand normalized integer-pattern vectors in \(\mathbb R^{13}\), such as permutations and sign choices of \((\pm1,\pm1,0,\ldots)\), \((\pm2,\pm1,0,\ldots)\), \((\pm1,\pm1,\pm1,\pm1,0,\ldots)\), and similar low-support patterns; greedily select points minimizing the incremental maximum inner product, followed by swap moves in which a selected point participating in a maximal pair is replaced by the pool candidate giving the lowest global maximum. Use cached pool-to-selected Gram matrices to make selection fast, then continuously relax the resulting discrete code with annealed softmax optimization and one final LP polish under a strict 160-second internal cutoff.

idea: Balanced annealed LogSumExp Riemannian Adam from the incumbent with cheap short-anneal screening of worst-pair micro-kicks and hole reinsertions, then a long equalizing anneal and brief LP squeeze.

Balanced annealed LogSumExp Riemannian Adam from the incumbent plus shake-and-repolish basin hops and greedy worst-point hole reinsertion to equalize the single-pair bottleneck, finished with a short high-sharpness squeeze.
Target-feasibility squared-hinge Adam below the record with successive lowering targets and kicked restarts, screened by exact Gram max and gated LP polish.
direction: Replace direct minimization of the maximum by target-feasibility optimization below the record. Set successive targets such as \(t=0.2068,0.2060,0.2050\), and minimize a tangent-projected squared-hinge loss \(\sum_{i<j}\max(\langle x_i,x_j\rangle-t,0)^2\) with Adam, starting both from the record and from moderately kicked copies with kicks \(0.05\)–\(0.15\). Unlike LogSumExp minimization, this objective penalizes every violating pair and permits motion through regions where the current maximum temporarily worsens, potentially dissolving the present contact graph. Whenever a target is reached, lower it and continue; screen trials using only the exact Gram matrix, apply LP polishing only to a configuration whose raw maximum is below \(0.2074344\), and stop all exploration by about 145 seconds.

idea: Prime cyclic Z73 Fourier-orbit search with simplex weight optimisation then symmetry-breaking polish.
direction: Search the untried prime-order cyclic family \( \mathbb Z_{73}\): generate all 73 points as one Fourier orbit with coordinates \(\bigl(r_m\cos(2\pi mk/73+\phi_m),r_m\sin(2\pi mk/73+\phi_m)\bigr)_{m=1}^6\) plus a common last coordinate \(h\), where \(\sum r_m^2+h^2=1\); phases cancel in pair products, so the score is just the maximum of 36 lag cosines \(h^2+\sum_m r_m^2\cos(2\pi ml/73)\). Globally optimise the six weights \(r_m^2\) and \(h^2\) on the simplex with differential evolution (population 30, at most 400 cheap generations) followed by Nelder–Mead minimax polishing, expand the best orbit, then break symmetry with perturbations of sizes \(10^{-4},10^{-3},10^{-2}\) and run short full-space LSE-LBFGS plus a 15 s LP polish for each, always retaining the incumbent if none beats \(0.2073372218913\).

idea: Use LP-dual tangent resultants to target unbalanced points for topology-changing kicks with short LSE+LP screening.
direction: Use LP-dual stresses to make targeted topology-changing kicks rather than random shakes: build the near-contact graph at slack \(3\times10^{-6}\), solve the trust-region LP, extract pair multipliers \(\lambda_{ij}\), and compute for each point the tangent resultant \(R_i=\sum_j\lambda_{ij}(x_j-\langle x_i,x_j\rangle x_i)\), which should vanish at a balanced optimum. Kick the 3–8 points with largest \(\|R_i\|\), explicitly including points 4 and 22, along \(\pm R_i/\|R_i\|\) and along random tangent directions orthogonal to \(R_i\), with angular sizes \(10^{-4},3\times10^{-4},10^{-3},3\times10^{-3}\); after each kick run only a short LSE anneal (\(\alpha=200\to2000\)) and LP repolish, accepting the result only if the exact maximum improves, with a hard 120 s search cap and incumbent fallback.

idea: High-precision active-set equiripple SQP polish of the incumbent with 5e-6 band LP tangent steps and trust-region backtracking.
direction: Perform a high-precision active-set SQP/equiripple polish of `best.npy` only, with no basin hopping: repeatedly take all pairs within \(5\times10^{-6}\) of the current maximum (cap 2500 by slack), solve the tangent-space LP \(\min t\) subject to the linearised pair constraints and \(\langle x_i,\delta_i\rangle=0\), add a small proximal term or trust radius scheduled \(3\times10^{-5}\to10^{-8}\), retract to the sphere, and accept only exact decreases in the true maximum after a short backtracking line search. Continue past the usual stopping point until at least the top 200 slacks are below \(10^{-10}\) or 140 s elapse, tracking LP dual multipliers and returning the best exact iterate; this directly tests whether the \(10^{-6}\) band can collapse into a lower, many-contact local optimum.

idea: LP-dual stress-directed topology kicks on the highest-resultant points plus short LSE anneal and LP repolish with strict improvement acceptance.

Thorough trust-region LP minimax polishing to reach a truly jammed equiripple optimum plus topology-changing hops (Gaussian shakes and worst-point hole reinsertion) repolished by short Adam then LP.
High-precision active-set equiripple SQP polish of best.npy with 5e-6 band, tangent LP and trust-radius backtracking to collapse the slack band.
direction: Perform a high-precision active-set SQP/equiripple polish of `best.npy` only, with no basin hopping: repeatedly take all pairs within \(5\times10^{-6}\) of the current maximum (cap 2500 by slack), solve the tangent-space LP \(\min t\) subject to the linearised pair constraints and \(\langle x_i,\delta_i\rangle=0\), add a small proximal term or trust radius scheduled \(3\times10^{-5}\to10^{-8}\), retract to the sphere, and accept only exact decreases in the true maximum after a short backtracking line search. Continue past the usual stopping point until at least the top 200 slacks are below \(10^{-10}\) or 140 s elapse, tracking LP dual multipliers and returning the best exact iterate; this directly tests whether the \(10^{-6}\) band can collapse into a lower, many-contact local optimum.

idea: Combine a cheap Z73 Fourier-orbit simplex search with unbalanced-pair basin hopping and short annealed Riemannian-Adam plus selective trust-region LP squeezing.
direction: Search the untried prime-order cyclic family \( \mathbb Z_{73}\): generate all 73 points as one Fourier orbit with coordinates \(\bigl(r_m\cos(2\pi mk/73+\phi_m),r_m\sin(2\pi mk/73+\phi_m)\bigr)_{m=1}^6\) plus a common last coordinate \(h\), where \(\sum r_m^2+h^2=1\); phases cancel in pair products, so the score is just the maximum of 36 lag cosines \(h^2+\sum_m r_m^2\cos(2\pi ml/73)\). Globally optimise the six weights \(r_m^2\) and \(h^2\) on the simplex with differential evolution (population 30, at most 400 cheap generations) followed by Nelder–Mead minimax polishing, expand the best orbit, then break symmetry with perturbations of sizes \(10^{-4},10^{-3},10^{-2}\) and run short full-space LSE-LBFGS plus a 15 s LP polish for each, always retaining the incumbent if none beats \(0.2073372218913\).

idea: Large-basin hopping with fast LogSumExp Riemannian descent from fresh and heavily-shaken starts plus a final high-precision LP equiripple squeeze to build a balanced contact graph.
Frozen-core triple surgery on low-degree holes with quasi-random greedy seeding and short LSE L-BFGS restarts plus time-boxed LP polish.
direction: Redo hole surgery as a small, strictly time-boxed frozen-core problem designed to avoid the previous timeouts: load and safeguard the incumbent first, remove only \(k=3\) points chosen from combinations of the active pair and the lowest near-contact-degree points at slack \(10^{-5}\), freeze the remaining 70, and optimise the removed triple jointly against the frozen core and each other using 8192 Sobol/quasi-random sphere samples for greedy seeding followed by at most 20 short LSE-LBFGS restarts (\(\alpha=300\to5000\)). Check the clock inside every optimisation loop, stop all surgery by 110 s, insert the best triple only if the full exact maximum improves, reserve the final 30 s for one LP polish, and otherwise return the untouched incumbent.
